items.title: Mrs. Cozzy Cary Interview, 1960-10-27
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, yeah. I sing Dr. Watts. ... Well, yes, they just, it's the name they call Dr. Watts. Well, it's just a long meter. A long meter is Dr. Watts.

ctx.x: All right. Let's see. We're talking to Ms. Elmore here right now. So we want to get when you were born and where. Well, I was born in 1902 in St. Mary Parish in a place called Glencoe, Louisiana, out from Franklin. That's near Baldwin or on the other side? Yeah, right near Baldwin. I know Jack Wilman from there. Jack Wilman, yeah. He's from Baldwin. Were you brought up in a church? You must have been. Yes. Which church was that? Methodist, ME. But I'm African Methodist now. You were just ME in those days? Uh-huh.…
Oh, yeah. I sing Dr. Watts.
Well, what, what are Dr. Watts hymns? What's, what does that mean?
